name: Cocoa powder (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Cocoa powder [Cocoa and cocoa products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 169593 (SR Legacy: Cocoa, dry powder, unsweetened) - full macro/AA/mineral/vitamin/fatty-acid panel
Holm et al. 1993, J Sci Food Agric doi:10.1002/jsfa.2740610111 (organic acids in fermented cocoa)
Oxalate in cocoa powder, Food Res Int 2011 doi:10.1016/j.foodres.2011.03.011 (total 650-783 mg/100g DM)
Li et al. 2012, Food Res Int doi:10.1016/j.foodres.2011.03.008 (acetic acid predominance / alkalization effect)
Fang et al. 2020, Food Sci Nutr doi:10.1002/fsn3.1701 (sugar/AA changes during fermentation)
Goude et al. 2023, Food Systems (cocoa organic-acid/sugar profiling)
provenance.curation_notes: Cocoa powder is a fermented-then-roasted, defatted concentrate: dominant growth-relevant carbon/energy sources are its abundant amino acids (protein 19.6 g/100g; Glu, Asp, Leu, Val highest) and organic acids (citric, lactic, acetic, oxalic ~0.7 g), NOT free sugars (only ~1.7 g total). Cocoa butter (13.7 g fat) is chiefly stearic + oleic + palmitic acid. Exceptionally mineral-dense (K, Mg, P, Cu). curation_added: palmitic acid (C16:0) - major cocoa-butter fatty acid, was absent
stearic acid (C18:0) - co-dominant cocoa-butter fatty acid, was absent
L-valine, L-phenylalanine - abundant amino acids absent from FooDB list
citric acid, acetic acid, lactic acid, oxalic acid - organic acids (fermentation-derived), all quantified
individual free sugars (sucrose/glucose/fructose) split from total
full USDA vitamin & mineral panel with amounts

curation_removed.name: Cholesterol
curation_removed.reason: Animal sterol, biologically implausible in a plant-derived cocoa powder; FooDB predicted, not a real cocoa nutrient.

curation_removed.name: L-Ascorbate (vitamin C)
curation_removed.reason: USDA FDC 169593 reports 0 mg vitamin C in cocoa powder; not a growth nutrient here.

curation_removed.name: Vitamin D
curation_removed.reason: USDA reports 0 IU vitamin D; absent in unfortified plant food (FooDB predicted).

curation_removed.name: Cyanocobalamin (B12)
curation_removed.reason: USDA reports 0 ug B12; plant food contains no cobalamin.

curation_removed.name: Retinol
curation_removed.reason: Animal-form vitamin A; USDA vitamin A = 0 in cocoa powder; implausible in plant food.

curation_removed.name: Beta-Carotene
curation_removed.reason: USDA vitamin-A/carotene activity ~0 in cocoa powder; negligible, not a growth-relevant nutrient.

curation_removed.name: Iron (Fe3+) / Fe2+ mitochondria / Iron (duplicate entries)
curation_removed.reason: Redundant iron speciation/compartment tags from FooDB; consolidated into a single 'iron' component (13.86 mg/100g).

curation_removed.name: Cobalt (Co2+)
curation_removed.reason: Trace non-nutritive element; not a quantified growth nutrient of cocoa (retain only if a Co/B12 source is explicitly required).

curation_removed.name: D-Serine
curation_removed.reason: Corrected to L-serine; D-enantiomer is not the protein-derived form present in cocoa.

composition_provenance.definition: sourced = the cited source states this component; derived = the pipeline supplied it. Classification table: tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
